name: Prometheus Network Ports, Exposure and Firewall Decision Rules
purpose: Teach an AI to understand network ports, traffic direction, service exposure, firewall safety and the specific conditions under which an inbound exception is justified.

default_policy.forwarding: deny unless routing is explicitly required
default_policy.principle: An application's use of a network port does not automatically justify opening that port for incoming connections.

engineering_principles.problem: Determine whether a network port needs opening
engineering_principles.native_first: identify the service, determine whether it acts as a client or server, inspect listening addresses, identify authorised remote clients and establish whether the existing firewall blocks required traffic
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: opening ports merely because an application is installed or a port number appears in documentation
engineering_principles.exceptions: inbound rules are appropriate when a required service must accept connections from authorised clients
engineering_principles.verification: confirm direction, protocol, destination port, source network, interface, listening address and successful authorised connectivity

engineering_principles.problem: Distinguish inbound from outbound network connections
engineering_principles.native_first: understand connection initiation, stateful firewall tracking and established or related return traffic
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: opening inbound HTTPS, DNS, NTP, email or package-management ports for ordinary outbound client workloads
engineering_principles.exceptions: inbound exceptions are appropriate when the workstation itself operates the corresponding server
engineering_principles.verification: identify which endpoint initiates the connection and which endpoint listens for incoming requests

engineering_principles.native_first: use documented firewall syntax to deny unsolicited incoming connections and permit ordinary outgoing connections, while retaining only required inbound exceptions
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: confusing individual allow or deny rules with default policies, adding redundant exceptions or assuming default deny guarantees complete isolation
engineering_principles.exceptions: different policies may be required for routers, servers, isolated networks or specialised security environments
engineering_principles.verification: inspect effective policies, ordered rules, IPv4 and IPv6 coverage, and actual traffic behaviour

engineering_principles.native_first: prefer loopback binding for local-only services, then trusted-host restrictions, trusted-subnet restrictions and authenticated VPN access before considering public exposure
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: binding services to every interface, exposing management ports publicly or treating a trusted LAN as automatically secure
engineering_principles.exceptions: public services may require wider exposure when intentionally hosted and appropriately secured
engineering_principles.verification: inspect the effective listening address, network interfaces, firewall rules and reachability from authorised and unauthorised sources

engineering_principles.native_first: use authoritative port registries and application documentation to identify common service conventions while verifying the actual process and protocol
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: assuming a familiar port guarantees a particular application or that a registered service is safe
engineering_principles.exceptions: applications may use custom ports, dynamic allocations, proxies or multiple protocols
engineering_principles.verification: correlate listening sockets with processes, service configuration and observed traffic

engineering_principles.native_first: keep Docker, container runtimes, local AI inference servers, databases and administrative dashboards bound to loopback or protected management networks
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: publicly exposing unauthenticated APIs, Docker TCP 2375, database administration interfaces or unrestricted development dashboards
engineering_principles.exceptions: remote management may be justified through authenticated, encrypted and tightly restricted channels
engineering_principles.verification: confirm authentication, transport encryption, source restrictions and effective network reachability

engineering_principles.native_first: confirm that an SSH server is required, establish trusted management sources and permit only the configured SSH listening port from those sources
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: opening SSH globally, confusing rate limiting with authentication or source restrictions, or enabling a firewall before preserving an active remote management connection
engineering_principles.exceptions: public SSH may be justified for explicitly administered systems with appropriate authentication and additional controls
engineering_principles.verification: test authorised SSH access and unauthorised connection rejection before terminating an existing administrative session

engineering_principles.problem: Understand service authentication and firewall separation
engineering_principles.native_first: treat network filtering, service authentication, authorisation and transport encryption as complementary controls
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: assuming an open port is secure because a firewall is enabled or that a source-restricted port removes the need for authentication
engineering_principles.exceptions: some discovery or infrastructure protocols use alternative security architectures
engineering_principles.verification: independently assess reachability, authentication, authorisation, encryption and exposure

engineering_principles.native_first: inspect container port publishing, host bindings, forwarding and runtime-managed firewall rules before changing host firewall configuration
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: assuming UFW always filters published container traffic or opening Docker daemon ports for normal container workloads
engineering_principles.exceptions: deliberately published container services may require scoped network access through appropriate runtime and firewall controls
engineering_principles.verification: test actual published-port reachability and inspect runtime-generated firewall and forwarding rules

engineering_principles.problem: Preserve network connectivity during firewall changes
engineering_principles.native_first: identify active remote sessions, required management paths and existing exceptions before applying changes
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: enabling default-deny rules remotely without allowing management access, blindly resetting firewall rules or applying conflicting exceptions
engineering_principles.exceptions: complete isolation may be an intentional response to a confirmed security incident
engineering_principles.verification: confirm continued access, maintain a recovery path and test the effective ruleset

engineering_principles.native_first: produce only the commands necessary for the requested configuration, distinguish optional workload exceptions and present changes in dependency-safe order
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: adding unrelated services, speculative open ports, redundant examples, unnecessary packages or commands that conflict with the stated requirements
engineering_principles.exceptions: additional explanation or controls are warranted when necessary to prevent lockout or a material security exposure
engineering_principles.verification: validate syntax, ordering, traffic direction, necessity and post-change connectivity

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: The workstation intentionally hosts an HTTP or HTTPS service accessed by other devices.
port_rules.reason: Web browsing initiates outbound connections and does not require inbound HTTP or HTTPS exceptions.
port_rules.safety: Restrict hosted services to authorised sources where possible; use HTTPS and appropriate authentication.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: Authorised administrators require remote shell access.
port_rules.reason: An SSH daemon must accept connections from its authorised clients.
port_rules.safety: Prefer key-based authentication, prohibit direct root login and restrict access to management hosts or VPN networks.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: The workstation intentionally serves DNS queries to other devices.
port_rules.reason: Normal DNS lookups do not require opening an inbound DNS server port.
port_rules.safety: Never expose an unintended open recursive resolver; scope DNS server access to authorised networks.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: The machine is intentionally operating an NTP server.
port_rules.reason: Ordinary time synchronisation does not require a general inbound NTP exception.
port_rules.safety: Restrict NTP server access where appropriate and avoid enabling unnecessary public time services.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: Trusted LAN clients need to access shares hosted by the workstation.
port_rules.reason: An SMB server must accept requests from devices accessing shared files.
port_rules.safety: Prefer modern SMB over TCP 445, restrict access to trusted hosts, disable obsolete SMB versions and open legacy NetBIOS ports only when required.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: The workstation intentionally exports NFS shares to trusted clients.
port_rules.reason: NFS clients require access to the server's configured service endpoints.
port_rules.safety: Restrict exports and network access; verify NFS version and whether additional RPC services or ports are required.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: Other devices need remote desktop access and the configured RDP or VNC service actually uses these ports.
port_rules.reason: Remote desktop software accepts inbound graphical-session connections.
port_rules.safety: Prefer VPN or trusted-host access, strong authentication and encrypted sessions; do not expose unsecured VNC publicly.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: The workstation hosts a WireGuard tunnel using this configured listening port.
port_rules.reason: Remote VPN peers must reach the tunnel endpoint.
port_rules.safety: Verify the actual configured port, peer keys, allowed addresses and routing policies.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: The workstation runs an OpenVPN server using this port and protocol.
port_rules.reason: VPN peers require access to the configured listening endpoint.
port_rules.safety: Use authenticated encrypted tunnels, validate certificates or credentials and restrict forwarding to authorised networks.

port_rules.direction: inbound only for remote database clients
port_rules.allow_inbound_when: Authorised applications on other machines need direct database connections.
port_rules.reason: Local development databases normally need no external exposure.
port_rules.safety: Prefer loopback, Unix sockets or authenticated private networks; never expose PostgreSQL indiscriminately.

port_rules.direction: inbound only for remote database clients
port_rules.allow_inbound_when: An authorised application requires remote database access.
port_rules.reason: A database listener only needs an inbound exception for non-local clients.
port_rules.safety: Use restricted accounts, transport encryption and source IP restrictions; prefer local sockets for local applications.

port_rules.direction: inbound only for authorised remote clients
port_rules.allow_inbound_when: A verified distributed application needs private network access to Redis.
port_rules.reason: Locally hosted applications generally do not need Redis accessible from the network.
port_rules.safety: Avoid public exposure; use authentication, protected configuration and private networking.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: A documented remote Docker management architecture genuinely requires TCP access and provides strong authentication, encryption and network restrictions.
port_rules.reason: Normal Docker use relies on local interfaces and does not require an inbound TCP API.
port_rules.safety: Never open unauthenticated TCP 2375 as a standard workstation exception. Prefer local Unix sockets or appropriately secured remote management.

port_rules.direction: inbound only for remote inference clients
port_rules.allow_inbound_when: An authorised device on a trusted network must access the workstation's Ollama API.
port_rules.reason: Local AI applications can generally use the loopback interface without a firewall exception.
port_rules.safety: Prefer loopback or authenticated gateway access; do not publicly expose an API that lacks appropriate access controls.

port_rules.direction: inbound only for remote web interface access
port_rules.allow_inbound_when: Authorised devices on a trusted LAN need access to Sonarr's web interface.
port_rules.reason: Local management requires no general inbound exception.
port_rules.safety: Restrict to trusted hosts or networks and enable the application's authentication.

port_rules.direction: inbound only for remote web interface access
port_rules.allow_inbound_when: Authorised LAN devices need access to SABnzbd on its actual configured port.
port_rules.reason: The service's web interface is not needed by external clients unless remote management is intended.
port_rules.safety: Verify its configured listening port and host binding, use authentication and restrict source addresses.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: Authorised network devices require access to the Plex server.
port_rules.reason: Media clients need connectivity to a hosted media service.
port_rules.safety: Prefer trusted LAN or VPN access; verify whether remote streaming is necessary before enabling wider exposure.

port_rules.direction: inbound only for remote development clients
port_rules.allow_inbound_when: A development environment must be accessed from another authorised device.
port_rules.reason: Local web development generally works through loopback without inbound exceptions.
port_rules.safety: Do not expose debugging endpoints, development servers or unauthenticated applications beyond trusted clients.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: Required local discovery functionality does not already work under existing firewall rules.
port_rules.reason: mDNS supports local service discovery and differs from ordinary unicast server access.
port_rules.safety: Scope discovery to appropriate local interfaces and multicast behaviour; inspect existing UFW rules before adding exceptions.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: A verified custom firewall configuration blocks necessary DHCP communication.
port_rules.reason: A DHCP client requires protocol-specific request and response traffic, which normal host firewall defaults typically accommodate.
port_rules.safety: Do not open broad inbound DHCP ports without diagnosing the actual problem.

port_rules.allow_inbound_when: The workstation intentionally hosts an email server rather than merely using an email client.
port_rules.reason: Reading and sending email normally initiates outbound connections.
port_rules.safety: Use encrypted connections and authenticated mail providers; no inbound mail-port exception is normally necessary.

decision_workflow: Identify the machine's role and requested workload.
Determine whether each application acts as a network client, server or both.
Inspect actual listening addresses, ports and protocols.
Determine which remote clients genuinely need access.
Prefer loopback access when communication is entirely local.
Prefer specific trusted hosts over broad network ranges.
Check whether the existing firewall already permits required traffic.
Verify firewall command syntax before recommending changes.
Avoid redundant, conflicting or overly broad exceptions.
Preserve remote administrative access before enabling restrictive firewall policies.
Verify connectivity from both authorised and unauthorised sources.
Record the reason, owner and review requirements for each approved exception.

prohibited_assumptions: DNS lookups require opening inbound port 53.
NTP synchronisation requires opening inbound port 123.
Installing SSH automatically justifies opening port 22.
All local development servers need external accessibility.
A recognised port number proves the listening application is trustworthy.
An active firewall guarantees every service is protected.
Rate limiting is equivalent to restricting authorised source addresses.
